reason: XnView MP already opens my pictures fine and I do not feel a few tens of milliseconds. I would open a cbz or two in NuViewer out of curiosity, then go back to what I know.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers are the headline, and speed is exactly what I would not notice on a double-click from Explorer. It also adds a gallery, an editor and a screenshot importer, which is more than I want from a viewer, and I already have a browser and batch converter in XnView MP. The one thing I would check is how it handles big zip/cbz files and huge folders, but a version 0.4.1 from one developer is not enough reason to move my default over.
current_app_pros: XnView MP is a browser, batch converter and metadata tool in one, handles my huge folders, and I know where everything is. It opens nearly every format I own and it is free for personal use.
current_app_pains: Nothing that bugs me enough to switch. It is a bit heavy and the interface is busy, but I have lived with that for years.
objection: The speed difference is a few tens of milliseconds and I would not feel it. A new single-developer viewer gives me nothing I miss, and I would have to redo my file associations by hand.
would_change_my_mind: Proof that it opens and pages through big cbz/zip archives and huge folders clearly faster and more smoothly than XnView MP, with a plain viewing mode and nothing else in the way.
